(1) BYOD adoption in SMEs is a complex phenomenon and (2) BYOD adoption is influenced by the SMEs’ characteristics, the SMEs’ employees, and the SMEs’ environment.
The BYOD phenomenon in SMEs in the developing world is not only a technological innovation but also a cultural innovation.
the SMEs in our study were not using BYOD but were willing to do so if they had the resources to support it.

understanding how BYOD is perceived in SMEs in a developing country context.
the contextualization of BYOD phenomenon in SMEs in a developing economy context.
investigating the adoption of BYOD by SMEs in the context of developing economies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BYOD phenomenon in SMEs in a developing country context is not well understood.
BYOD is a phenomenon that has the potential to significantly impact SMEs in developing economies.
there is a need for SMEs in developing economies to embrace BYOD in order to remain competitive and relevant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BYOD can be beneficial for SMEs in developing economies.
the SMEs are more likely to adopt BYOD in developing countries than in developed countries.

the BYOD phenomenon can be contextualized in SMEs in the developing world, but the contextualization will require a different lens from the developed world and the large organizations.
